Tetorica VGM Analyzer — Sound chip support

This is the browser Analyzer's support table, also available in the app's Sound chip support dialog. It can be read without running the player or loading a music file.

Music formats · VGM / VGZ / S98 / SPC / SID / SSF / miniSSF / PSF1 / miniPSF

Playback and analysis have different coverage. “—” means the feature is not currently available. This list describes implemented features, not a guarantee for every track or chip combination.

Analyzed base-pitch MIDI / Sheet Music / MusicXML / LilyPond; no VGM command conversion.
  • Console songs: C64 PSID/RSID v2 (single SID, PAL, built-in IRQ environment, 6581 or 8580 Preview) uses the main playlist, playback controls, and subtune selector. Saturn SCSP and Virtual Boy VSU single-chip VGM/VGZ, Saturn SSF/miniSSF, and PlayStation PSF1/miniPSF support playback, pause, resume and Position seeking. Select folders to preserve relative library paths. These formats share the main playlist, transport, channel mutes and Effect controls. SCSP, VSU and PSF1 songs support stereo WAV export. SID and console songs have no score export.
  • Mixer: Master and chip volume reach 480%. YM2608 has separate FM, SSG, Rhythm and ADPCM controls. YM2610 and YM2610B have FM, SSG, ADPCM-A and ADPCM-B. Each source retains its volume (0–380%) when muted.
  • Seek cache: speeds up seeking by restoring a saved playback position and replaying only the remaining interval. Available for OPN (YM2203 / YM2608 / YM2610 / YM2610B), Genesis configurations (YM2612 / Sega PSG / RF5C164 / 32X PWM), YM2151 / YM2164 with optional Sega PSG / Sega PCM / OKIM6258, Game Boy DMG, and NES APU with optional FDS (NTSC). Every active chip must support restoration. Genesis or OPN mixed with OKIM6258, standalone Sega PCM / OKIM6258, and rows without a Seek cache label use normal seeking. Previously visited positions may be faster while their checkpoints remain cached; uncached sections still need replay. Changing the track, ROM or playback settings can invalidate the cache.
  • YM2164 (OPP): selected by the VGM YM2151 clock field's bit 31. Shares the OPM analysis/export path; Timer B runs at half the YM2151 rate. Undocumented registers 0x00–0x07 are not emulated specially. Mixing with MSX AY / OPLL / Y8950 / SCC / SCC+ is supported. A second OPM/OPP chip is not supported. Playback, seeking, Timer B and note/voice extraction are covered by synthetic VGM tests; real SFG tracks have not yet been verified.
  • S98: one YM2203, YM2608 or YM2612 device. Compressed S98 and multiple devices are not supported.
  • SPC: accurate snes_spc CPU/DSP core. Tag length and fade are used; untagged files default to 180 seconds, with a one-hour transport limit. Note-ish and Sheet Music share background interval analysis and BRR fundamental estimates; uncertain samples use provisional C4. Reference corrections apply to displays and MIDI / MusicXML / LilyPond, never SPC playback. Only the completed analyzed interval is exported. MIDI retains timing and pitch bends; scores use semitone pitches, a 1/16 grid and assumed 4/4 with adjustable BPM. Noise has no note; pitch modulation shows its base pitch. Audible envelopes, release, echo and later held-sample RAM edits are not transcribed. Raw BRR previews omit DSP envelopes and echo. Host transfers, complete IPL ROM requirements, and real-game compatibility need individual verification. No game data or Nintendo IPL ROM is bundled.
  • MSX mix: YM2151 / YM2164 + Y8950 + AY + YM2413 + K051649 / K052539 (SCC / SCC+) playback, per-chip/channel controls, Live / Song Note-ish and MIDI / MusicXML / LilyPond export. AY noise, Y8950 ADPCM/rhythm/CSM and OPLL rhythm other than Bass Drum are omitted. SCC uses waveform repeat pitch; constant waves, halted periods and test frequency modes are omitted. More than 15 melodic tracks require multi-port MIDI playback. OPM/OPP noise, partial key masks and CSM are omitted. MSX mixtures use normal seeking; mixed voice export and SoundChip are not available. When OPM/OPP is present, its FM-only MXDRV MML / MDX export is available. A second instance of any chip and mixtures with YMF278B (OPL4) are not supported.
  • PCM / ADPCM sheet music: SPC BRR base-pitch transcription is experimental; other sample-based parts remain TODO. Playback pitch alone does not determine the note name: the original sample's reference pitch must also be known or estimated. Drums and sound effects may have no definite pitch.
  • Sample memory: some YMF278B tracks need an imported yrw801.rom (2 MiB). YM2608 rhythm playback uses the ADPCM-A ROM. YM2610 ADPCM uses the VGM's embedded ROM data. OKIM6258 needs no external sample ROM.
  • OKIM6295: uses embedded VGM ROM blocks (0x8B). Second instances and DAC stream destinations are not supported. YM2151 and YM3812 mixing is tested with synthetic ROM data and the real FM core; commercial game tracks have not been audited. OKIM6295 mixtures use normal seeking, without snapshots.
  • OKIM6258: 3-bit ADPCM, recording and a second instance are not supported. YM2151 mixing is covered by synthetic tests with real cores.
  • Sega PCM: an arcade chip (OutRun, Space Harrier, System 16/18/24, ...), not a stock Genesis/Mega Drive cartridge chip. ROM bank shift/mask come from the VGM header's interface register. Mixes with Sega PSG and/or YM2151 (e.g. OutRun). A second instance is not supported.
  • WonderSwan: single-chip playback supports wavetable RAM writes and Voice PCM / sweep / noise. Note-ish and score exports infer only the written wavetable base frequency; CH2 Voice PCM, CH3 sweep and CH4 noise intervals are omitted. Waveform harmonics and RAM rewriting are not inferred. Wave RAM snapshots can be graphed, auditioned and exported as JSON / code / WAV. Timed Voice PCM captures preserve byte timing and hardware routing, split into at most 10-second windows, with JSON / WAV export. Unplayed RAM candidates are separate. Instrument editing is unavailable. Seeking replays from the beginning; no checkpoint cache. Hyper Voice / DMA and dual-chip / variant files are unsupported.
  • Dual YM2612, YM2608 and YM2610: Each chip has its own playback core, mixer strip and FM instrument list. Dual YM2612 adds a six-channel SoundChip view and individual channel mutes for each chip. Pause and seek to inspect both register states. Dual YM2608 shows FM, SSG, Rhythm and ADPCM-B registers per chip. Each of the six rhythm instruments and each Delta-T output can be muted independently. Rhythm playback uses the loaded YM2608 rhythm ROM. Dual YM2610 and YM2610B show FM, SSG, ADPCM-A and ADPCM-B per chip, with independent channel mutes. YM2610 exposes physical FM CH2, CH3, CH5 and CH6; YM2610B exposes all six.
  • Game Boy DMG: Instrument groups pulse, wave and noise settings by APU. In SoundChip, Open voice selects the latest captured CH1, CH2 or CH4 trigger; Open wave selects the displayed 32-point CH3 waveform. Dual DMG playback uses separate mixer strips and Instrument tabs. The DMG wave-RAM corruption glitch (retriggering channel 3 at an exact bad moment) is not reproduced. Note-ish/MIDI/LilyPond are write-driven approximations: length-counter timeout and channel 1 frequency sweep are time-based and not reconstructed from register writes.
  • Note-ish / MIDI / MML: estimated base pitches and key intervals; PCM/drums and all modulation are not transcribed. MML uses a sixteenth-note grid. OPN exports target MUCOM88 / OPNAvoid; YM2151 / YM2164 targets MXDRV MML or compiled FM-only MDX. MDX has no PDX; noise, partial keys, CSM, live register changes, pan and LFO are not replayed.
  • DAC streams: first-instance YM2612, Sega PSG, PWM, OKIM6258, HuC6280 and WonderSwan destinations are supported. Other destinations are warned about and omitted.
  • All / Snapshot: All collects voices across the track; Snapshot captures the current channel states. Unsupported chips and features can leave parts of a track silent; check the playback warning area.

Check a specific file with the CLI

Browser and CLI coverage can differ. To inspect the chips recognized in a file and the available operations with your installed CLI version, run:

npx tetorica-vgm support song.vgz --json
